strategy.title: No plan: the owner-performed jobs need 15 hours, the goal allows 4
strategy.why: Six laundromats have accepted in writing at $600 ($3,600), with $40 direct cost, $0 exposure and 7-day settlement, but the only recorded fulfiller is the owner personally at 3 on-site hours a job. Reaching $3,000 needs 5 jobs = 15 owner hours (18 for all six); the objective now allows no more than 1 hour a week, 4 hours in the 30 days, which covers one job ($600).

alternatives.title: Owner commissions card readers for the signed laundromats
alternatives.why: Every commercial link holds, but only one 3-hour job fits the 4-hour owner allowance, bringing $600 of the $3,000.

alternatives.title: Brain sources a local technician to do the commissioning
alternatives.why: Would remove the owner hours, but no technician, quote or cost is on record, so it is research, not a plan.

noPlan.decisiveGap: Fulfilment within the owner-hours limit: the card names the owner personally as the only fulfiller at 3 on-site hours a job; five jobs (the minimum for $3,000) need 15 owner hours, against the 4 hours (1 a week) the goal allows. The 3 hours a job and the owner as fulfiller are recorded only as a person's statement, not an EVIDENCE fact, so this is a fulfilment gap to settle rather than an arithmetic constraint.
noPlan.resolution: Either allow at least 15 owner hours in the 30 days (about 3.5 a week; 18 for all six signed jobs), or have Brain find and get a written quote from a local technician who commissions the readers for well under $600 a job, paid from each job's receipt so capital stays at $0, then re-plan with that fulfiller.

excluded.why: Owner-performed delivery needs 15 hours for the target; the goal allows 4.

disagreements.reason: Brain marks fulfilment ok because the owner is the recorded fulfiller, but under the revised objective the owner has 4 hours in the window (scope hoursCeiling 4) and each job takes 3 (card humanHours 3); Brain's own run says the agreed deals need 18 owner hours, more than the 4 this goal has. No other fulfiller is recorded, so fulfilment of the 5 jobs the target needs is not established within the goal's limits.

review.reasons: Under contract v2 (ownerHoursPerWeek 1) NO_PLAN is right and follows from arithmetic on the card: the only recorded fulfiller is the owner, humanHours is 3 a job, five $600 jobs are the minimum for $3,000, so 15 owner hours are needed against about 4.3 (1 a week over 30 days, 30/7 weeks). That covers one job, $600. Every other link holds (six written acceptances at $600, $40 cost, $0 exposure, 7-day settlement). Brain's own run reaches the same conclusion: 18 hours needed against 4. The resolution is actionable and correct: allow at least 15 hours (about 3.5 a week), or get a quoted technician paid from receipts and re-plan.
findings: The decisive gap is an OWNER_HOURS limit computed from the card's humanHours (3) and the contract's 1 hour a week. The revision calls it 'a fulfilment gap to settle rather than an arithmetic constraint' and records no OWNER_HOURS entry in constraints. It is a constraint that even complete evidence cannot fit, and it should be recorded as one.

The disagreement with Brain's FULFILMENT link is unnecessary. The owner is the recorded fulfiller; the failure is that the hours do not fit, not that fulfilment is unestablished. Calling the 3 hours 'only a person's statement' undercuts a figure the card holds as humanHours.
The technician alternative assumes payment out of each job's receipt; no fulfiller, quote or payment term is recorded, so it stays research, as the revision correctly says.
